names.conventions: Thais carry a given name and a family name, given first. Family names only came in with the Surname Act of 1913, and each new surname had to be unique to its family, so they are long, often Pali or Sanskrit in origin (Wongsawat, Srisuk) and two strangers rarely share one. People are addressed by the given name with Khun in front, never by the family name. Almost everyone also has a short childhood nickname (chue len), often an English word or a single sound (Bank, Ploy, Nok, Mint), and that is what friends, colleagues and vendors use, with Phi or Nong in front by age. Many Thai Chinese families kept a Sae- surname from their clan (Saetang, Saelim), though most took Thai surnames, sometimes built on the clan name (Tangsakul). The 'also' lists are common nicknames.
